title: The Painter and the Farmer
lines: Nell lives on a farm with her dad.
Her dad is a farmer with a big barn.
The paint on the barn was cracked and gray.
Nell said it made the farm look sad.
First she got a brush and some soap.
She stood on a box and did her best.
But the gray did not come off at all.
So they got a painter to fix it up.
The painter came out from the city in a van.
She had just red paint in the back.
She painted the barn red from top to bottom.
"All barns look like that," said Nell.
Then Nell had a much better plan.
"Can you paint a big picture on it?"
The painter was an artist as well.
She made a farm and a big sun on it.
Nell held the paint pots for her all day.
Dad was cross at first, but now he grins.
A visitor comes out each day to look.
Nell tells them her dad has the best barn.

questions.ask: What was wrong with the barn at the start?
questions.listenFor: The paint was cracked and gray, and Nell said it made the farm look sad.

questions.ask: Whose plan was the big picture?
questions.listenFor: Nell's. She is the one who asks the painter to paint a big picture on it, in line fourteen.

questions.ask: Would you paint your house a picture or one plain color? Why?
questions.listenFor: Either answer is fine. The reason is the point.
